ceiling_directive: Replace the endogenous all-order plane restriction with a primitive d-factor intervention mechanism, prove that it implies the required cumulant geometry on a nondegenerate class, and establish the weak-flag lower bound over that same class.
improvement_directive: Derive the condition \(u_k\in\operatorname{col}(c_2,\ldots,c_{d+1})\) from an explicit primitive environment-shift model rather than imposing the identifying cancellation geometry directly. Then extend the matching weak-flag lower bounds from the single engineered experiment to the resulting primitively defined shell class.
critique: The quotient identification is proved only under the load-bearing all-order restriction that every latent cumulant-shift vector lies in the plane generated by the observed low-order treatment contrasts; the note gives constructions satisfying this condition but does not derive it from a natural primitive model. The advertised if-and-only-if frontier is confined to a union whose no-breakout branch is defined by requiring the legal unequal-effect swap that supplies nonidentification, so it is not a characterization of the broader simultaneous-shift model. The TL;DR's claim of sharp weak-flag rates on bounded shells overstates the theorem: uniform upper bounds hold for arbitrary fixed admissible classes, while matching lower bounds and the consistency converse are proved only for one specially constructed compatible experiment. These restrictions leave the contribution specialized and limit its practical relevance, particularly because the proposed Sachs application supplies no evidence that the latent-plane condition holds. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
